nodes.recap: chapter header + waking alone in metal cell
nodes.text:
-------------------------------
|          CHAPTER 18          |
-------------------------------


$CA voice calls your name without quite pronouncing it.##

Insistent, anxious, almost frightened, hovering somewhere just above
the surface of your unconsciousness, a pulsing pink halo of light
that your mind has been dreaming as a sound.##

You realize you are waking up. And then, all at once, the last moments
on the ship rush back: the sea's tremendous fury that would not let up,
the instant of panic when the water poured into the hull
as the vessel capsized, and then darkness.# And then nothing.##

You sit up sharply, and in the pitch black you slam your head
violently against something metal above you.# A piercing pain
rings through your skull and you press a hand to your forehead,
cursing under your breath.# You sit up more slowly,
extending your hands above you.##

Your left hand goes instinctively to your hip.# The sword is not there.
Neither is the knife.##

A metallic click, and a hum.# Whatever that sliding sound is,
it is the door opening,
and in the doorway a dark silhouette blocks a harsh light from behind.
$D"$CBring him with the others.$D"$C A voice, flat, not quite human.##

Hands seize you, bind your wrists, blindfold you, and drag you
in a direction you cannot map.##

nodes.recap: brought to the scientist's viewing room - first sight of the mutant
nodes.text:
After several minutes of walking, you are shoved into a seat.
Someone removes the blindfold.##

As your eyes adjust, you see that the others are all here,
on chairs like yours, and the relief of that is physical.#
Smiurl is pale to the point of translucency, Corolla already
studying the room with her fighting mind, Theo rigid with readiness,
Efeliah watchful and still.#
All of them. Nobody missing.##

You are in a large room whose entire front wall is one vast window.
Beyond it, the sea floor, lit from somewhere below,
where pale creatures drift through dark-blue water
and the pressure must be crushing.# Equipment and instruments
and screens cover every other wall, and a figure stands with its back to you
at a desk of buttons and lights.##

It wears a white coat.# It cannot be human:
from the back of its head, blue-gray cartilaginous appendages
descend behind its shoulders, like the memory of fins.##

When it turns, you see the face: the same blue-dark, greenish color.
Not a hair on it, no nose, no ears, only flat smooth skin
where those features should be, with small holes in their place.
The eyes are disproportionately enormous, and the mouth has no lips.
The hands and feet are webbed.##

It studies you all, and makes an expression you cannot read.
Efeliah's voice arrives in your minds.##

$g<<It finds us disgusting.# Repellent.>>$C##

$c<<Charming. And it's quite the looker.>>$C

nodes.recap: scientist declares intent - Efeliah taken to the psi-sonde room

dialogues.precomment: The creature speaks in a guttural, slurring voice.
dialogues.line: It says: 'I think you will prove useful to us.'
dialogues.comment:
It gestures, and others like it appear, taller,
moving with a boneless fluidity, who simply take hold of you
and drag you apart. It takes two of them to move Theo,
though they are bigger than him and enormously strong.
One lifts Kriss like a wooden puppet.##

Efeliah's voice rings in your minds, alarmed.

dialogues.line:
They want to run experiments on all of us.#
That one must be their leader, or a scientist of some kind…

dialogues.precomment: The scientist-creature speaks again, and you hear behind you the voice you woke to.
dialogues.line: The female. The fairer one. For the psi-sonde.
dialogues.comment:
You see them take Efeliah into another room.##

A moment later, the rest of you are thrown into a metal cell.
The door slides shut behind you.##

Kriss recovers his balance and immediately throws himself at the door,
kicking and pounding it, shouting.

nodes.recap: cell - Ef's warning from the other room, Smiurl's lore

dialogues.precomment: You hammer the door until Efeliah's voice stops you cold.
dialogues.line: Ef! Efeliah! We have to get her out!

dialogues.precomment: Her voice arrives in your minds with a steadiness that costs her something.
dialogues.line:
They want to probe my mind.# They have identified unusual faculties in me.
The instrument is crude, I think.# It could damage me.##

I don't know how long I can hold out.#
And when they are done with me, they will begin with you.
We have to get out of here.
dialogues.comment: You say it to the cell, to the door, to whoever has an answer.

dialogues.line: We can't leave Ef in the hands of these fish-men.

dialogues.precomment: Smiurl is standing very still, staring at nothing, his skin a stunned gray.
dialogues.line: The sea mutants…
dialogues.comment: He says it almost to himself, distracted.

dialogues.line: What?

dialogues.precomment: Smiurl does not answer immediately. After a moment he begins, slowly.
dialogues.line:
My grandfather used to tell me the history of our people, when I was small.#
There is something that has come back to me just now.

He said our race was created by the people from Earth
through manipulation of the genome of normal men.#
But alongside ours, other races were created too.#
One of them was that of the mysterious sea mutants,
whom we believed to be a legend…
You mean these monsters were grown in a test tube?
dialogues.comment: Smiurl darkens, and Corolla sees it at once.

dialogues.line: I'm sorry.

dialogues.precomment: He waves it away, though it has landed.
dialogues.line:
Leave it. It doesn't matter.##

But yes: they are modified-DNA beings,
and I'd wager that like my people they can reproduce naturally.##

The story said, also, that those men without morals wanted
to create intelligent beings capable of living in hostile environments,
like the sea floor. To exploit the energies and resources
hidden in the planet: that was their purpose.##

They say they built a submarine city from which one could access
the fire beneath the earth beneath the sea.
Converting the thermal energy of the mantle into electricity.
What?

If it's as Smiurl says, and if this is the submarine city,
it can only be a geothermal plant.# Thalassothermal, maybe.

dialogues.precomment: Smiurl resumes his recitation as if reading from somewhere inside himself.
dialogues.line:
The sea mutants can live underwater as easily as in the air,
and they are endowed with extraordinary strength…
dialogues.comment: Efeliah's voice cuts through, tight with strain.

nodes.recap: Ef's pain builds - Kriss's rage - the door-punch
nodes.text:
$g<<They are about to begin attacking my mental defenses.#
I don't think I can hold out long…>>$C##

A sensation of suffering accompanies the words,
not described but transmitted, Efeliah's actual pain
arriving in your chest the way her voice does, directly.##

Kriss, the moment that pain reaches him, feels himself go cold with fury.
He begins to pace the narrow cell, his footsteps ringing sharp on the metal.##

$B"We have no weapons."$C#
Theo watches him, almost as if he can hear his thoughts.##

$Y"And they're strong,"$C# Smiurl confirms, deflated.##

You breathe out hard. The helplessness is unbearable.
Corolla watches you with understanding, having no better answer.##

$c<<Maledizione.>>$C# You plant yourself in front of the door
and shout it aloud too.

$C"$cMaledizione!$C"##

You close your eyes. You clench your fists.##

You think of Efeliah on the other side of that wall, suffering,
who could be dying or worse from one moment to the next,
who has always been close to you,
closed to each of you. You think of the sword you don't have,
of Theo's hammer you don't have, of the door that cannot be opened.#
This cannot end here.##

You can feel Efeliah's suffering growing, her mind stiffening
in the effort to resist.# You no longer feel anything around you.
You are alone, in nothing, with your rage and her voice in your skull.##

It happens in an instant.# Without realizing what you are doing,
you begin to scream, and your hand snaps forward
as if it were your sword,
struck the door with all the force of desperation.##

A detonation fills the room.###

You open your eyes.# The door is against the opposite wall,
and two guards are pinned beneath it, motionless.
The metal is twisted at the exact point where your fist connected.##

Your head swims. Colored lights streak past your vision.
Your hand is bleeding, but after a moment you can move it.##

You stand perfectly still, trying to understand what just happened,
and cannot, and then the others push past you
and take the guards' weapons from the floor.##

nodes.recap: they arm up and go find Ef
nodes.text:
$Y"Come on, Kriss!"$C Smiurl, already in the corridor.##

Theo is examining the guards' weapons: electric prods,
two acuminate electrodes between which a visible shock crackles
when you press the button. He hands both of them to Corolla.
For himself he picks up a long metal tube wrenched free from the door by the impact.##

$B"Let's go."$C##

You retrace the corridor you were dragged down, and open the door
through which you saw Efeliah disappear.
Another corridor opens ahead.# You move from door to door,
each in turn, until you hear Efeliah's muffled voice and the voices
of mutants somewhere ahead.##

Theo kicks the door open and is inside before it finishes moving.#
His tube descends on the first mutant who blocks him,
caving the skull.# Corolla throws a prod at a second, pinning it
to the wall with lethal precision, then wheels and drives her second prod
into a third one's throat, dropping it when the current
flows through its body.##

You grab the weapon of one of the fallen
while your companions are still fighting,
and slide around behind the scientist-creature,
who stands frozen, watching the scene.##

nodes.recap: Kriss uses the scientist as hostage to free Ef

dialogues.precomment:
An alarm begins to wail somewhere in the walls.##

The scientist turns and sees you behind it, the prod leveled.
dialogues.line: They'll be here soon and you'll all be dead.
dialogues.comment: The scientist mutant speaks, guttural, slurring.

dialogues.line: I don't care!# Free her immediately, or I plant this thing in your gills!
dialogues.comment:
A pause, in which the mutant calculates
that in any case compliance is the sensible option.##

It nods.##

You watch the sensors attached to Efeliah's skull and body,
where she lies stretched on something resembling an operating table,
retract instantly into their housings.# She sighs.# After a moment
she opens her eyes, and slowly sits up.

dialogues.precomment: Her voice is quiet, composed, but barely.
dialogues.line: More are coming.
We need weapons.
We need a way out.
dialogues.comment: Kriss drives the prod into the scientist's back.

dialogues.line: Where are our weapons?!

dialogues.precomment: The mutant says it does not know. Kriss shoves the electrodes into its flesh.
dialogues.line: Tell us!
dialogues.comment: The mutant gasps, then says, breathless:

dialogues.line: Perhaps. In the minisub area.
Can you get us there, Ef?
dialogues.comment:
She holds still for a moment, searching something in the scientist's mind.##

$g<<Yes.>>$C

nodes.recap: running through corridors with hostage - toward the diaphragm door
nodes.text:
$B"Walk."$C# Theo, to the scientist, flat and absolute.##

$c<<You had better walk.>>$C# You press the prod to its back.
$C"You'll want to move quickly."

From the staircase to their right,
a heavy trampling of feet, growing louder.##

You run left.##

Efeliah runs point with Corolla at her shoulder,
wounded but barely showing it, ready to strike.
Theo and you drag the scientist between you.
The alarm has not stopped; the whole base is ringing with it,
and ahead and behind the sound of running feet echoes
through the metal corridors.##

At a junction, Efeliah stops before a massive circular metal door.##

She stands before it for some seconds, saying nothing,
then takes the scientist's hand and presses it flat against
a plate at the center of the door.# The plate brightens at the touch,
and the door slides open silently, irising apart,
revealing a long glass tunnel ahead.##

$c<<Fingerprints.# Or something like them.>>$C##

You push through. Efeliah closes the door behind you.##

$g<<It can only be opened by those with sufficient standing in their hierarchy.#
They should not be able to follow.>>$C##

You do not ask what that means, because there is already shouting
on the other side of the door, and no time to weigh it.##

nodes.recap: the glass tunnel - city glimpsed on the run
nodes.text:
The walls of the tunnel are glass.##

You are already running when you understand this,
and you do not stop, cannot stop,
but you see it as you run: a long crystal tube
connecting two structures, and beneath it, dozens of meters down,
the sea floor, lit as bright as noon, sprawling out
for the area of a small city in every direction.##

To the left: mutants at work, emerging from minisubs without any protection,
at ease in the water as you are in air, digging or preparing
some new structure, deliberate and purposeful.#
To the right, you see something more extraordinary.##

A city.##

A real city, streets and gardens of algae and coral,
and around what might be a market
a great number of mutants move with the unhurried purpose
of people who have somewhere to be.# Colorful structures
cling to the rock face like shells.# Small luminous submersibles
shuttle between points, ferrying passengers.##

And then, from a building, a crowd of small mutants pours out,
proportioned differently, their enormous eyes not yet fully developed.##

$g<<Children coming out of school…>>$C##

Efeliah says it with a particular hesitation.# Nobody says anything else.
You keep running, but you are all looking,
and the scientist-mutant you are dragging along has taken on
the expression of something like pride,
though it says nothing, not a syllable.##

$g<<They're entering the tunnel! We must keep moving!>>$C##

nodes.recap: scientist released - the flood trap begins
nodes.text:
The tunnel continues ahead in a straight line,
narrowing with distance into a point of darkness.##

After another minute of running, Efeliah says:
$g<<There is a slight downgrade ahead.>>$C# And then:
$g<<They are coming.>>$C##

You shove the scientist toward the tunnel wall
and release it.# It stands very still where you leave it,
watching you run, the pride-expression fading into something
you cannot name and do not have the time to study.##

You run.##

A few minutes in, you feel it: water under your feet.
Rising, not from above but creeping along the tunnel floor,
cold and inexorable.# You look back.
The scientist has closed its mouth into something like
a sharp-toothed smile.##

$Y"They want to drown us,"$C# Smiurl says,
in a tone of simple, defeated fact.

You all look at Efeliah, who gives one short nod.##

$c<<Of course.# Of course they do.>>$C##

$c"Then there's no time to waste,"$C# you say.

You run harder.##

nodes.recap: water rises - the apnea choice
nodes.text:
The water rises faster the farther you go,
and the tunnel shows no sign of climbing.##

You wade through it at hip height.
Smiurl is already swimming.# The others follow.
You stop when there is only the thickness of a head between the water
and the tunnel ceiling, all of you treading,
and Theo says nothing because there is nothing useful to say.##

$R"What do we do?"$C# Corolla asks.##

$g"Look, the tunnel rises there,"$C# Efeliah says,
pointing ahead through the water: some meters forward,
the tunnel curves sharply upward into the rock,
climbing not quite as fast as it descended.
Beyond that point the water would be shallower again, or at least
the ceiling higher.# Then air.##

$B"You want us to swim it."$C# Theo, flat.#
Efeliah doesn't answer.##

$C"I don't think we have any other choice,"$C# you say.##

They all look at you, each of them deciding the same thing.##

$B"Smiurl goes first. Then Corolla. Then Ef. Then Kriss.# I am last."$C##

Smiurl draws up to the water's edge,
takes three, four, five deep breaths with an anguished expression,
and dives.# Corolla follows instantly, gone clean beneath the surface.##

nodes.recap: the apnea swim - two approaches
nodes.text:
Theo's hand finds your shoulder.##

$B"Stay close."$C##

Efeliah goes under.# You take your breath, the deepest you can,
and follow.##

The illumination of the tunnel carries through the water,
so you can see where you are going: the curve upward a dozen
meters ahead, the wavering green light above it,
the others' shapes moving through the dark.##

How do you approach the swim?

choices.desc: Long, steady strokes, measured, don't burn it all at once.
Go as hard as you can, straight to the surface.

nodes.recap: wrong choice - burned through air
nodes.text:
You go hard, everything at once, churning the water.
Twenty meters and your lungs are already screaming,
but the curve is just there, and past it the ceiling opens,
you can see the pale air above the waterline...##

You let go of the breath. The cold water fills your throat.
Your vision goes at the edges, gently, the way the sea does everything.##

The dark comes in like a tide.##

nodes.recap: the apnea swim - drowning - Theo resuscitates
nodes.text:
Long strokes, don't fight it.##

Every nerve in your body wants speed, but you know,
you know the way your lungs know, that burning the air early
gets you nowhere. You measure it out,
stroke by stroke, the burning growing and being set aside,
the curve arriving, then past it, the ceiling higher now,
the green light of the air above closer with every pull.##

Ten meters. Five.##

Your lungs give out on you.##

You don't decide to let the air go.# It leaves,
and the salt water takes its place,
and you swallow it and your body
makes its own decision about what this means,
and the decision is that it is finished,
here on the bottom of an unknown ocean on this absurd planet,
and after everything, all the danger and the things witnessed,
this is the epilogue.# On Earth they must have given you up
as lost from the first day you disappeared.##

The darkness comes in from the edges.# In your chest, a strange heaviness.
With the last thread of consciousness you register
that this is your final moment.##

Then a great pressure on your chest.# Once.# Twice.# Three times.##

You open your eyes, gasping, coughing salt water from your lungs,
and Theo is there, squeezing you like a lemon
with his enormous hands, and when you have spat out the last drop
you drag yourself upright and look around.##

They are all here, all of them,
and their faces carry a fear you have rarely seen on any of them,
and Efeliah's breath is still short.##

You reach a hand to Theo.##

nodes.recap: after the drowning - no rest, press on

dialogues.line: If I'm alive, it's because of you.# You saved me.
dialogues.comment:
He grips your hand and allows himself a smile,
then pulls you to your feet.

dialogues.line:
We cannot stop even now.#
For them the water is no obstacle.

nodes.recap: out of the tunnel into the rock cavern
nodes.text:
You make for the portal at the top of the tunnel.##

This one has no protection. It opens docilely
with a hiss the moment you press the button.##

You step into a vast space, much of it carved from the rock itself.
An enormous hum fills it, and the smell of hot metal and electricity.
Countless pieces of equipment populate the cavern,
all of them active to judge by the noise and the light,
stacked without pause from floor to the high ceiling,
with metal walkways providing access to the upper ones.#
Two staircases rise left and right into corridors bored through the rock.##

nodes.recap: Theo divides the party - search for a way out

dialogues.precomment: Theo has already read the space.
dialogues.line: We should split up.# Smiurl, come with me.
dialogues.comment: He moves toward the right staircase.

dialogues.line: Find a way out. And our weapons.
I'll be the link between both groups.
dialogues.comment: She turns and runs left, with Corolla and Kriss behind her.

nodes.recap: the grotto with their ship being dismantled
nodes.text:
The left corridor is the same reddish rock,
electric cables strung between bulbs at regular intervals.
You follow it for a minute or two without meeting anything,
then it ends, opening onto a metal landing above a vast cavern.##

What you see stops the breath in your lungs.##

The ship.##

In the center of the cavern, an enormous grotto cut into the rock,
their ship lies at rest,
the one you sailed south on, the one that took you all down with it.#
Mechanical arms hiss and clank around the hull, the mast, the solar sails,
dismantling it piece by piece with methodical indifference.#
Already the forward half is in sections on the floor;
only the stern remains intact.##

You descend to explore, keeping your distance from the mechanical arms
that would crush you without noticing.##

Then a mutant stares down at you from a control booth
high on the cavern wall, frozen in surprise for a moment,
then recovers and reaches for something like a telephone.##

$R"It's calling reinforcements,"$C# Corolla says,
reading it the same moment you do.##

$c<<As if we didn't have enough problems.>>$C##

A hiss cuts the air between you, and something metal
stikes the floor just behind you.# The technician
that calls reinforcements also shoots at you with something like a harpoon gun.##

You run.##

nodes.recap: minisub dock found - Corolla clears it
nodes.text:
A side corridor, low and curved, takes you away from the harpoon darts.
At its end, an open door: and inside, a dock.##

Several minisubs rest in their berths,
low and sleek and entirely alien in design,
but real, and floating, and connected to the surface
by water that glints faintly far above.##

$c<<Our ticket to the surface.>>$C##

Two mutants emerge from behind a row of storage racks,
reaching for their own prods.#
They do not get the chance.# Corolla is already on them,
and within moments both are on the floor, and their weapons in her hands.
She assesses the two new prods with the air of someone
calculating how to operate four of a thing simultaneously.
She appears to conclude she can.##

$R"We need Theo and Smiurl."$C##

You double back toward the ship-grotto,
cautious around the mouth of the dock entrance.
The technician in his booth has vanished.##

$g<<They're coming!>>$C##

A mass of mutants pours into the grotto from the same corridor
you used. And from the upper walkways, more.##

nodes.recap: battle in the ship grotto - Theo and Smiurl arrive
nodes.text:
Corolla goes to ground behind a segment of the ship's hull,
already toppled with the rest of the prow.
$R"Get to the control booth! I'll draw them off!"$C##

You take cover behind whatever the dismantling arms have left.
Efeliah moves for the booth, low and fast.
Her voice arrives in your minds:
$g<<I will try to confuse their minds.# Hold as long as you can.
Theo and Smiurl should arrive any moment.>>$C##

The first attackers to reach you find that the ship wreck and the
moving machinery between you and the main group cost them time
they do not have.# But the rest begin to fan out,
trying to flank.# Three reach Corolla; others come for you.##

You have no sword. Your borrowed prod is not the weapon you know.
But the cavern has a floor,
and it has cables, and it has machinery that moves,
and you use all of them.##

encounter.victorymessage:
$CTheo drops from the upper platform at full height
and takes three of them down before they have seen him,
and Smiurl comes behind him scattering blinding light
from every inch of skin.# The result is brief and conclusive.##

Your weapons are in Theo's hands.# And then in yours.#
You draw the sword and look at your reflection in the blade,
steady and certain, and step forward.##

A few minutes later it is finished.
Efeliah descends from the booth.

$g<<We should go before more arrive.>>$C
encounter.defeatmessage:
$CThey are too many, and they do not stop,
and eventually Corolla's prods run dry
and your prod finds no target that stays down.##

The scientist will get its experiments after all.##

nodes.recap: Kriss figures out the minisub controls
nodes.text:
You pile into the largest minisub and Smiurl seals the hatch.##

$R"Who knows how to pilot this thing?"$C#
Corolla gestures at the control board.##

$g<<I have never seen anything like it.#
And I don't have a pilot nearby to borrow from.>>$C##

You lean in over the controls.#
Amidst a field of blinking indicator lights, two things stand out:
a device that looks precisely like the joystick from your computer at home,
and a flight-style control stick beside it.
All the labels are in characters you cannot begin to decipher.##

You sit in the pilot seat.# You ease the control stick
lightly upward, and a low vibration runs through the hull.##

$c<<Can't be that complicated.>>$C# You say it partly for their sake.##

You study the central lever: it can slide vertically.
You lower it a few millimeters.##

The minisub tilts, then begins to descend slowly toward the dock water.##

$Y"How do you do that?!"$C# Smiurl, delighted despite everything.##

$c<<This one controls the drive motors,>>$C# you say,
$c<<and this lever here is for diving and surfacing.>>$C##

$Y"What about those?"$C# He points at the twin joysticks.##

$c<<Still working on that.>>$C##

$B"Two swiveling propellers,"$C# Theo says, from over your shoulder.
$B"Should have about ninety degrees of rotation."$C##

You test it.# The minisub yaws, first right, then left.##

$Y"What did I tell you?!"$C# Smiurl shrieks with what passes for joy in a near-death situation.##

Guide channels of pale light mark the path to the cavern mouth.
You push the throttle forward.##

$c<<Only one thing we still don't know,>>$C# you say,
as the rock walls accelerate past either side,
$c<<is how this thing brakes.>>$C##

nodes.recap: surfacing - orientation - Smiurl's navigation trick
nodes.text:
You burst from the cavern into open water at full speed.
The minisub wobbles, finds itself, and angles sharply upward.##

When you break the surface, actual sunlight comes through the viewport,
and everyone goes quiet for a moment at the fact of it.#
You think about embolism for a second, then Smiurl opens the hatch
and takes a breath and is perfectly fine,
and you close that particular worry in a drawer at the back of your mind
where it will stay until you have time to look at it properly.##

A collective silence, then a general eruption of relief that is partly noise
and partly just the absence of dread.##

The only problem is that there is nothing to eat or drink aboard,
and the water they have between them is very little.##

$R"Which way do we go?"$C# Corolla at the compass.#
$R"The cardinal points don't match anything I know."$C##

$g<<I have no idea where we are.>>##

$c"We need to go south,"$C# you say.##

$R"And how do we know which way that is?"$C##

You had been about to suggest waiting for night
and navigating by the stars, when Smiurl squeezes past you
and sticks his head through the hatch for a moment, then drops back in.##

$Y"South is that way,"$C# he says, pointing slightly to your right.##

$R"And how exactly would you know?"$C# Corolla, genuinely surprised.##

$Y"Simple.# The sun is low on the horizon.
If the city at the bottom of the sea keeps solar time, that's west."$C##

Nobody says anything.# You all look at Smiurl.##

$c<<Right. Of course. The dwarf.>>$C##

You turn the minisub to Smiurl's south.#
That night, when the stars come out, you check,
and he is exactly right.##

nodes.recap: Efeliah's revelation - the storm was artificial

dialogues.precomment:
The night passes in shifts at the controls.
By morning, when you are all awake,
Efeliah speaks.# She has been quiet since the tunnel,
quieter than usual, and there is something in the way she chooses
her words now that tells you she has been sitting with this for hours.
dialogues.line: There is something I need to tell you.
Go on.
The storm that sank us.# It was not a natural phenomenon.
dialogues.comment: She lets that sit a moment.##

dialogues.line: And who...

The mutants.# The complex of machines we saw inside the structure
where we found our ship: that was only part of an enormous machine
capable of controlling the weather.# I read it in their minds.##

They detected us somehow, at a distance.
They sank us deliberately.#
Getting possession of that ship was one purpose,
but capturing living human specimens, especially ones with unusual mental faculties,
was the real prize.# They would have run every kind of experiment
on our minds and bodies.
That's not possible.
All that seawater must have gone to their brains!
dialogues.comment:
He says it with a righteous indignation
that is so precisely correct that everyone laughs,
half from the joke and half from the pure physical relief
of having escaped people who would have done exactly that.##

And then you stop laughing, because you find yourself looking back,
in your mind, at the city in the glass tunnel.
The children coming out of school.
The market, the coral gardens, the little luminous submersibles
plying their routes. The scientist in his white coat,
holding his arm after what Efeliah told you, looking
at something you still cannot name.##

The scientist who found you disgusting.# Who you found disgusting.##

nodes.recap: closing reflection - 'those mutants are no less human than us'
nodes.text:
$c<<Those mutants…# they are no less human than we are.>>$C##

You say it aloud before you have decided to.##

Nobody answers.# Nobody has the courage to add anything.##

The minisub runs south, its motors quieter now,
and ahead of you, the sea.##
